summary.headline: UltraTech Q2 FY27: volumes up 13.8% with 71% utilisation; trade prices exited September ~3% above Q1 average and are about 5% above Q2 average.
summary.overview: Management described a quarter where a weak monsoon kept construction active, while a West Asia conflict pushed fuel costs higher. Q2 trade prices averaged roughly 1-1.5% below Q1 on a soft August, but rose sharply in late September and October. Volume growth of 13.8% ran ahead of an industry estimate of about 10%, and net profit rose 21% YoY. Fuel cost per bag rose to INR 51.5 from INR 45, and the company expects the price increases to flow mainly into Q3 earnings.

financial_highlights.change: absolute fixed costs up 4% vs volume +13.8%

segments.name: Cement - regions
segments.commentary: North grew over 20% and South 15-20%; East ~5%, West ~10%, Central ~10%. Utilisation was above 70% in North and South, about 70% in West, and about 60% in Central and East.

segments.name: Wires and Cables (Ultravolt)
segments.commentary: Launched 3 September 2026 with INR 1,800 crores planned capex, of which INR 1,100 crores is spent or committed. Production of house wire, panel wire and multicore cable has started; power and control cable lines are due in H2. Management says it is too early to judge revenue or margins; it is a division, not a subsidiary.

guidance_outlook: Trade prices exited September at least ~3% above Q1 average; October prices are about 5% above Q2 average, with management expecting more increases in the next couple of months.
Full benefit of price increases expected in Q3 earnings rather than immediately, given festive-season slowdown.
FY27 capex guidance held at about INR 10,000 crores (plus or minus), with a fuller view after Q3.
Net debt/EBITDA expected below 1x by end-March 2027.
Fuel cost guidance: INR 2.1/kcal may rise to about INR 2.2/kcal, assumed to hold for H2 if pet coke stays near $180/tonne; management expects only a marginal Q4 impact from current inventory.
Business-as-usual delivery of the INR 1,400/tonne EBITDA exit-March-2028 target, with cost pressures expected to be covered by price increases.
Expects industry volume growth of about 8% in H1 FY27 and very strong momentum to March 2029.
Ultravolt: a mature business expected in FY28; April-June 2027 quarter is flagged as one worth discussing.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 4.6 Mtpa in September, taking domestic cement capacity to 204.7 Mtpa, including the 3.6 Mt greenfield plant at Petnikota (Andhra Pradesh) and 1 Mt of debottlenecking at 3 units.
On track for 240 Mtpa as planned; next phase of organic growth to be announced, with North capacity expansion plans to come before end-FY27.
Added 116 MW renewable power and 10 MW waste heat recovery; 47% of power from non-fossil sources; 2 GW green power for captive use.
Thermal substitution rate about 7.2% after AFR systems commissioned at 2 plants.
Ultravolt plant at Jhagadia (Gujarat); 1 main warehouse, 5 regional distribution centres and about 16 branch warehouses.
India Cement kiln shutdowns planned for upgrades (WHRS, preheater height) with benefits expected from Jan-Mar 2028 quarter.
demand_pricing: Q2 average trade prices were 1-1.5% below Q1 owing to a soft August; prices rose 7-10 per bag month-on-month in the second half of September, with non-trade prices higher.
Mumbai prices rose 3-4% per bag; South showed the strongest momentum in prices, volumes and utilisation.
Trade ratio stable at 65-67%; industry sales were 463 Mt in FY26 against UltraTech's 145 Mt.
Management says the industry is now sold out, so pricing is leading volume.
Domestic coal is constrained because Coal India prioritises the power sector; pet coke was about $180/tonne, and pet coke share was cut to about 25%.
Rural demand may soften in some areas; the company cites weak monsoon, drought in pockets and farm-income risk.
UBS network above 25% of trade sales, with about 6,500 stores targeting 10,000 by FY28-29.
Ultravolt pricing is at market parity; the company says differentiation comes from premium Class 5 HR/FR products.

qa_highlights.question: What cost inflation is expected in H2 from current spot levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not forecast peaking. The fuel kcal cost may go from INR 2.1 to INR 2.2, which is assumed to hold if nothing else changes; marginal Q4 impact expected from inventory.

qa_highlights.question: How big is the price increase versus the Q2 average?
qa_highlights.answer: Spot realisation is about 5% above the Q2 average, with September and October combined.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt rose QoQ; why?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by capex and the dividend payment. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x from 0.94x at March 2026, and management expects it below 1x by March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest costs rise about 22% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 5,000 crores of NCDs at 7.25% were raised and held for about 2 months.

qa_highlights.question: Will Ultravolt's capex go beyond INR 1,800 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: No sanction beyond INR 1,800 crores. Management says the ramp-up is the focus and that the revenue target could reach INR 16,000-18,000 crores on copper prices, against the earlier INR 10,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Will the industry return to pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says pricing is leading, the industry is sold out, and the price increases will cover cost pressures.

qa_highlights.question: Will the EBITDA per tonne target of INR 1,400 hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Business as usual, with cost pressures covered by price increases; management confirmed delivery of the INR 1,400 commitment.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: pet coke, imported coal and industrial diesel costs are elevated, and any escalation adds to H2 cost pressure.
Whether October price increases hold through the festive slowdown and are absorbed in Q3.
Rural demand softening after a weak monsoon and drought pockets; household inflation.
Ultravolt: early-stage, with ramp-up, dealer stabilisation and margins unproven; revenue and utilisation not yet disclosed.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; the company targets below 1x by March 2027.
Eastern markets (Bihar, West Bengal) still underperforming with utilisation near 60%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pricing and the South region, but evasive on forward cost curves, fuel contract terms and Ultravolt numbers, which were deferred to later quarters. Management said H2 will not be free of cost pressure.
key_quotes: We exited September in trade at least about 3% above the Q1 average.
Our capacity utilization was 71%, better than 66% last year on a higher base.
Business as usual is what my expectation is to deliver that INR1,400.
I won't pretend that second half will be free of cost pressures.

growth.why: Volumes grew 13.8% YoY (vs industry ~10%) with utilisation at 71% vs 66% LY; the 4.6 Mtpa commissioned in September and the price increases (October ~5% above Q2 average) support growth, though no explicit revenue growth % was guided and the 240 Mtpa next phase lacks announced timing.
